label: Networking
opening: It's your first week on the network team at **<<biz>>**. Every site has switches, Wi-Fi and cables, and today nobody knows which ones are close to full. The team lead wants a program that watches the whole estate.
rule: A switch has **<<level>> ports**. A site with <<level>> devices or fewer fits on one switch. A bigger site needs another, before devices start dropping off the network.
scene: A colleague pings you: "How many devices are at <<n2>>?" Nobody should have to read the whole report. The monitor needs a quick lookup, and it must cope with sites you don't manage.

action.name: needs_second_switch
action.doc: say whether the site has outgrown one switch

glossary: A box that connects wired devices on one network. Each cable uses a port.
A socket on a switch. A 24-port switch connects 24 devices.
How much data a link can carry, measured in Mbps.
Megabits per second, the usual unit for network speed.
The most traffic a site is likely to need at once.
The share of time a service is working. Monitors exist to protect it.
The delay before data starts to arrive, in milliseconds.
py_uses: Automate router and switch configuration across hundreds of devices
Ping every device and alert when one stops answering
Parse network logs to find the cause of an outage
